lines.text: Many learners say: Can you borrow me your pen?
Better: Can you lend me your pen?
You lend to a person. You borrow from a person.
Lend! Can you lend me some money?

data.wrong: Can you borrow me your pen?
data.right: Can you lend me your pen?
data.why: You lend to a person. You borrow from a person.

native.tip: « Prêter », c’est “lend”, et « emprunter », c’est “borrow”. On ne dit pas “borrow me”, on dit “lend me”.

en.tip: Say “lend” when you give something for a short time, and “borrow” when you get something for a short time.
en.caption: Do you say this? “Can you borrow me your pen?” Say “lend” when you give something for a short time, and “borrow” when you get something for a short time. Say “Can you lend me your pen?” Listen to Ama and repeat with her! More exercises in the Lexkite app.
